event: Nala wakes in room 7 and checks her hands first; they are still small, pale and freckled.
She fell asleep thinking of the Deep, and wakes glad to still be Nala, more glad than sorry.

memory.fact: Nala is glad to still be Nala, more glad than sorry.
Nala is glad to still be Nala, more glad than sorry.

event: Wren hammers on door 7 at first light: porridge, then the party, properly this time.
Over porridge the widow tells Wren to keep her boots off the table.
After porridge Nala and Wren go down Ladder Lane to the Brass Kettle to fetch Elowen.
Elowen is waiting outside the Kettle with a new box of chalk and a bundle of candles.
The three sit at the Kettle's corner table, empty at this hour, and talk it through.
Wren says how her party worked: finds split even, the scout goes first, nobody plays hero.

memory.fact: The party splits finds even, Wren scouts first, and nobody plays hero.
The party splits finds even, Wren scouts first, and nobody plays hero.
The party splits finds even, Wren scouts first, and nobody plays hero.

event: Wren asks what each of them can do.
Elowen says she can make light, and dress a cut or a bite with the herbs in her pouch.

memory.fact: Elowen knows herbs and simples from her mother, and carries a little pouch of them.

event: Nala says honestly that she can do nothing yet, but she can carry rope and read a map.
Wren says that is more than most coppers, and that she will teach them the rest.
Nala keeps to herself that she was Alan; she does not know how she would even say it.

memory.fact: Nala has told no one in Emberdeep that she was Alan.
Nala has told no one in Emberdeep that she was Alan.

event: Wren says they will go down today, just the first level, just to walk it and come back.
Elowen goes pale, then nods.
At the guild hall Wren rubs her own name off the party board with her sleeve.

memory.fact: The party board chalks up every party wanting hands, and every delver looking for a party.

event: She chalks the three of them up as a party: TOLLEY, MARSH, FAIRWEATHER.

memory.fact: Nala, Wren and Elowen are a party, chalked on the guild party board as TOLLEY, MARSH, FAIRWEATHER.

event: They cross Coppergate and walk in under the arch of the Mouth.

pictured.coverAfter: The light changes the moment you pass beneath it. The sun is behind you,
pictured.setting: the ramp and gate below the Mouth

event: Past the Mouth a broad worn ramp runs down into the dark, the daylight thinning behind them.

memory.fact: Past the Mouth a broad worn ramp runs down into the dark to the guild's gate.
Past the Mouth a broad worn ramp runs down into the dark to the guild's gate.

event: At the bottom of the ramp is the guild's gate, and a warden at a table with a big book.
The warden signs them into the Mouth book, a party of three, and notes the hour.

memory.fact: A guild warden at the gate signs every party in and out in the Mouth book.
A guild warden at the gate signs every party in and out in the Mouth book.

event: Wren tells them a party not signed out by the next morning is searched for.

event: Nala lights her tin lamp with clumsy fingers, and gets it on the second try.
Beyond the gate the dark is total and the air is cold and still.

memory.fact: The Deep has no light of its own; delvers carry lamps, and the air is cold and still.
The Deep has no light of its own; delvers carry lamps, and the air is cold and still.

event: Elowen takes Nala's hand without a word, and Nala lets her keep it.

pictured.coverAfter: The Long Hall opens up round you in the lamplight a little at a time.

event: The Long Hall opens up in the lamplight: dressed stone pillars marching away into the dark.

memory.fact: The Long Hall runs from the guild's gate, a pillared hall as long as Coppergate.

event: Wren says nobody knows who cut it; it was old before the town was built.

memory.fact: The first level is old dry halls and passages of dressed stone, cut by no one anyone knows.
The first level is old dry halls and passages of dressed stone, cut by no one anyone knows.

event: Wren teaches them to keep the lamp shuttered low and to stop when the scout stops.
Elowen chalks an arrow on a pillar pointing back to the gate, and Wren whoops at her.

memory.fact: Elowen's chalk arrows on every fourth pillar of the Long Hall point back to the gate.
Elowen's chalk arrows on every fourth pillar of the Long Hall point back to the gate.

event: Wren says chalk is the best thing a copper ever brought down, and Elowen glows.
Nala reads the map by the lamp, and finds the Long Hall's end and the turn to the Well Room.
A side passage the map marks uncertain is not where the map draws it; it has shifted.

memory.fact: The first level's side passages shift with the seasons, and the guild map marks them uncertain.
The first level's side passages shift with the seasons, and the guild map marks them uncertain.

event: Nala sees it first and says so, and Wren gives her an approving nod.

memory.fact: Nala can read a map, and spotted a shifted passage on the first level before Wren did.

event: The Well Room holds an old stone well; they drink, and the water is clean and very cold.

memory.fact: The Well Room holds an old stone well whose water is clean and very cold.

event: Wren shows them where to look for finds: rubble, cracks, the foot of a fallen wall.

memory.fact: Small ember-stones turn up in rubble and cracks on the first level, a handful on a good day.
Small ember-stones turn up in rubble and cracks on the first level, a handful on a good day.

event: They kneel in a rubble-choked side room and sift with their hands by lamplight.
Nala finds her first ember-stone in a crack: small, warm, glowing faintly orange.

pictured.coverAfter: The Well Room is square and high, and in the middle of it is a well.

event: She holds it up and laughs out loud, and it echoes down the passage.
Wren reaches into a deep crack for another stone, and a cave rat as big as a cat bursts out.

memory.fact: The first level's commonest creatures are cave rats as big as cats, and pale crab-like crawlers.

event: The rat bites Wren's forearm and is gone into the dark before anyone can move.
Wren swears long and inventively, and says it is nothing.

pictured.coverAfter: There's a side room off the Well Room, small and half-choked with rubble where
pictured.setting: the rubble side room off the Well Room

event: Elowen makes her sit on a block of stone and roll up her sleeve.
The bite is two deep punctures, bleeding freely.
Elowen washes it with cold water from the well, and packs it with a herb from her pouch.

memory.fact: Wren has a cave-rat bite on her forearm, dressed with Elowen's herbs.
Wren has a cave-rat bite on her forearm, dressed with Elowen's herbs.

event: Nala tears a strip from the hem of her shirt, and Elowen binds the bite with it.

changes.from: A plain shirt, a bodice laced up the front, a pair of breeches and boots, with a thin linen nightshirt.
changes.to: A plain shirt, a bodice laced up the front, a pair of breeches and boots, with a thin linen nightshirt. A strip is torn from the hem of the shirt to bind Wren's arm.

event: Elowen's hands are steady the whole time; afterwards she shakes, and laughs at her shaking.
Wren looks at the neat binding and calls Elowen a marvel, and Elowen goes red.
They keep sifting, more careful now, and Nala keeps her knife out to poke into cracks first.
By afternoon they have eight small ember-stones between them.
Wren leads them on to look at the far end of the level, past the Well Room.
At the far end, Wren shows them the head of the Dry Stair going down to the second level.

memory.fact: The Dry Stair, at the far end of the first level, goes down to the second.
The Dry Stair, at the far end of the first level, goes down to the second.

event: She says not today, and Nala is glad.
On the way back, in a narrow passage, pale crab-like crawlers spill out of the wall.
There are dozens, clicking, nipping at boots and ankles; one nips Nala through her breeches.
Nala's lamp is shuttered too low to drive them off, and she fumbles at the catch.
Elowen holds up her hand and calls her light, as bright as she has ever made it.
The crawlers scatter from the light and are gone into the cracks in seconds.

memory.fact: Cave rats bite and run; crawlers nip, and scatter from bright light.
Cave rats bite and run; crawlers nip, and scatter from bright light.
Cave rats bite and run; crawlers nip, and scatter from bright light.

event: Elowen stands there with her hand blazing white, breathing hard.
Wren says she has never seen crawlers clear off that fast.
Elowen lets the light go out and says she did not know she could make it that bright.

memory.fact: Elowen can make her light blaze white as noon, and did not know it until the crawlers came.
Elowen can make her light blaze white as noon, and did not know it until the crawlers came.

event: Nala tells her she was brave, and Elowen shakes her head, and then stops shaking it.
They follow Elowen's chalk arrows back down the Long Hall to the gate.
The warden signs them out of the Mouth book and notes the hour.
They climb the ramp into the last of the daylight, dusty and stiff and grinning.
At the finds market an ember-stone dealer buys their eight stones at two pennies each.

memory.fact: The finds market buys a small ember-stone for two pennies.

event: The dealer holds back a penny of the sixteen as the guild's tenth, and pays them fifteen.

event: Wren splits the fifteen pennies even: five each.

changes.note: Nala's even share of the fifteen pennies the eight stones fetch

event: Wren twists three of her five pennies into a scrap of cloth to send home to Saltby.
Nala asks; Wren says her family are fishers in Saltby, eight children, and she is the second.

memory.fact: Wren grew up in Saltby, a fishing village on the coast, the second of eight children.

event: At the Brass Kettle they eat supper, four pennies each.
Nala pays four pennies for supper, and has four left of the eight she held.

event: Elowen says tonight is her second of three nights paid at the Kettle.

memory.fact: After her second night at the Brass Kettle, Elowen has one paid night left.

event: Wren hears it and looks thoughtful, and keeps whatever she is thinking to herself.
Wren raises her mug to the party, and they drink to it.
Under the table Elowen's knee rests against Nala's, and neither of them moves away.

memory.fact: Nala and Elowen held hands in the Deep, and kept their knees touching under the table at supper.

event: Elowen goes up to her room under the eaves; Wren and Nala climb Ladder Lane together.
On the top landing Nala sees blood has soaked through the binding on Wren's arm.
Nala brings Wren into room 7 and sits her on the bed to change the binding.
Nala washes the bite in the basin, and tears a fresh strip from her nightshirt hem to bind it.

event: Wren is quiet for once, watching Nala's hands and then Nala's face.
Nala is very aware of Wren's bare forearm in her hands, warm and sun-browned.
Wren thanks her, gruffly, and says nobody has fussed over her since she left Saltby.

memory.fact: No one had fussed over Wren since she left Saltby, until Nala rebound her bite in room 7.

event: Wren ruffles Nala's hair on her way out, and says goodnight.
Nala lies in bed and turns over the day: the dark, the stone in the crack, the crawlers.
She thinks of Elowen's knee against hers, and of Wren's arm in her hands.
She falls asleep tired all through, in a good way she does not remember from being Alan.
